agree.reason: The email is direct and admits the evening shifts, which builds trust, but a long-serving teller who doesn't want phone work gets little reason to take the role beyond same pay and two days at home.

honest.reason: The brief's figures are reported accurately, but the one-on-one meetings 'in the next two weeks' are an invented commitment, and 'members who reach a real person faster' is stated as a result when no fact supports it.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated rather than worked out: there's no severance example (ten years comes to 20 weeks of pay), no note that the center's 12-hour day is 50% longer than the branches' 8 hours, and no explanation of what a 60% rise in contacts does to hold times if nothing changes.

right_comparison.reason: Falling visits and rising phone and chat volume are set side by side as a trend, but the email never says what happens if the branches stay open, so the staff's real alternative is only partly described.

qualification.reason: The announcement states firm decisions and offers, so it needs no conditional hedges.

objections.reason: It takes on the shift-rotation objection honestly but never addresses the central one, that these staff don't want phone work. It also ignores the two weeks of rumours and what long-tenured staff lose when their branch relationships end.

fit.reason: It's an email from the COO of roughly 420 words with clear sections, which matches the brief's form and length.
